text:
The Wild arrive in Boston with points in ten straight games (8-0-2) and a lot of noise around them that has nothing to do with the standings. Quinn Hughes's future is the story that won't go away: headlines this month ask whether he'll stay, and his extension talks haven't produced a deal. Minnesota is also the team most linked to Dylan Larkin, and Elliotte Friedman said this week he believes the Wild's offer for the suspended Detroit center is Danila Yurov and three first-round picks. Through all of it, the team keeps winning.

Jesper Wallstedt is the biggest reason. He's at .925 and 16.4 goals saved above expected this season, and over his last five starts (5-0-0) he's stopped .947. Kirill Kaprizov has points in ten straight (6 goals, 12 assists), and Matt Boldy scored a hat trick in Toronto on Thursday. The Wild's results run ahead of their chances (+24 goals on +17.4 expected), and that gap is goaltending, but the chances themselves are good: 56% of the expected goals during the streak. One worry: Daily Faceoff reported Joel Eriksson Ek left Thursday's game with an injury.

Boston is the league's other happy surprise, and a more fragile one. The Bruins are +23 in goal difference on only +1.5 expected; finishing (7.7 goals above what their chances usually produce) and goaltending (13.8 saved above expected) are carrying them. Jeremy Swayman is at +8.4. Montreal ended their four-game win streak 5-2 on Thursday, with Cole Caufield scoring again. James Hagens, twelve points in 17 games, is on injured reserve with a back injury (ESPN estimates Nov. 21). Since he went out, Marat Khusnutdinov has slid in beside Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt. Boston takes 4.8 penalties a game, which matters against a Minnesota power play that creates 0.90 expected goals a night.

Our numbers have Kaprizov at 46% to score and Boldy at 41%; David Pastrnak leads Boston at 30%. Minnesota won the first meeting 4-1 on Oct. 3. Our playoff odds: Wild 98.5%, Bruins 80%.
headline: Ten straight with points meets Boston's overachievers
